statements.markdown:
**Comparison with the same finite instance.** The concentration of the
finite maximum in §11.1.2 strengthens this to a near-optimal sampled
configuration. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is one finite
deterministic word $W$, independent of $n$ and $J$, such that
$$
\Pr_{J,\Sigma}\!\left\{
H_{n,J}(\Sigma)\ge\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)-\varepsilon n
\right\}\longrightarrow1.
$$
statements.section: 11.2 What is averaged, and a fixed-word probability consequence

statements.markdown:
To see this, choose the word with $v_W\ge P_*-\varepsilon/4$ and
write $r_n=\mathbb E(E_n-v_W)^2\to0$ and
$M_n=\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)/n$. The convergence
$\mathbb E M_n\to P_*$ makes its bias at most $\varepsilon/4$
for all sufficiently large $n$. The Gaussian coefficient-vector bound
from §11.1.2 and Chebyshev's inequality for $E_n$ then give, for $n\ge2$,
$$
\Pr_J\{M_n>P_*+\varepsilon/2\}
 \le2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n^2\varepsilon^2}{16(n-1)}\right\},
\qquad
\Pr_{J,\Sigma}\{E_n<v_W-\varepsilon/4\}
 \le\frac{16r_n}{\varepsilon^2}.
$$
Outside these two events, $M_n-E_n\le\varepsilon$. Their union
therefore has probability tending to zero. The maximum and the measured
energy use the same disorder, and the union bound needs no independence.

One fresh preparation and measurement suffices for this asymptotic
statement.
statements.section: 11.2 What is averaged, and a fixed-word probability consequence

statements.markdown:
**Corollary 6 (a measured configuration on the same instance).**
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a finite ordinary QAOA word
$W_\varepsilon$, chosen independently of $n$ and $J$, such that one
computational-basis measurement $\Sigma$ satisfies
$$
\Pr_{J,\Sigma}\!\left\{
\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)-H_{n,J}(\Sigma)\leq\varepsilon n
\right\}\longrightarrow1
\qquad(n\to\infty).                               \tag{14}
$$
statements.section: 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit

statements.markdown:
**Proof.** For a fixed word, put
$Y_n=H_{n,J}(\Sigma)/n$ and
$K_n=\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)/n$.
[Farhi, Goldstone, Gutmann and Zhou, §4, equations (13)–(22)][FGGZ]
prove
$$
\mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n\to v(W),\qquad
\mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n^2\to v(W)^2.
$$
The second moment is $\mathbb E_J\langle(C_{n,J}/n)^2\rangle$,
so it includes measurement variance as well as disorder fluctuations.
Thus $Y_n\to v(W)$ in joint $L^2$. Gaussian concentration of the
maximum and its defining mean limit give $K_n\to P_*$ in probability.
Choose $W$ with $P_*-v(W)<\varepsilon/3$. With probability tending
to one, both $K_n-P_*<\varepsilon/3$ and
$v(W)-Y_n<\varepsilon/3$, which proves (14). The two energies use
the same $J$, and the argument needs no independence between them.
statements.section: 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit
